articles.headline: Tottenham can't be ruled out of relegation dogfight - Joe Cole, Steven Gerrard
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur could find themselves in another relegation battle this season, according to Joe Cole and Steven Gerrard.
articles.headlineJa: トッテナムの降格争いの可能性は排除できない — ジョー・コール、スティーブン・ジェラード
articles.descriptionJa: ジョー・コール氏とスティーブン・ジェラード氏によると、トッテナム・ホットスパーは今シーズン、再び残留争いに巻き込まれる可能性がある。
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur could find themselves in another relegation battle this season, according to Joe Cole and Steven Gerrard.

Roberto De Zerbi saw his side slump to a 3-2 defeat at home to Aston Villa on Saturday, condemning the club to their worst-ever Premier League start after five matches.

Two late goals from Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul Van Hecke were Tottenham's first of the league campaign but weren't enough despite a summer of expenditure designed to take them clear of last season's 17th place finish.

"They have overpaid for every player that they bought this summer," Joe Cole said to TNT Sports.

"You can't rule them out of being in or around the relegation battle. They are not scoring goals, and they look so weak at the back."

Cole mentioned Van Hecke's inability to thwart Nicolas Jackson's goal for Villa: "[Van Hecke] scored the goal but he has to be disappointed with his performance.

"I know that the way they play leaves the centre-halves vulnerable but that's why you buy centre-halves who can deal with those one-on-one challenges. I know he's a handful, Jackson, but for the goal it's not good enough.

"I think they've got a real problem with -- forget scoring goals -- they look fragile, as well. Put the two together and it only comes up with one conclusion.

"This is going to be a long season for Tottenham."

Tottenham have finished 17th two seasons in a row in the Premier League despite winning the Europa League under Ange Postecoglou.

But they spent more than £300 million ($402m) this summer to back new coach De Zerbi who has just two points in five league games.

Steven Gerrard also worried about their relegation prospects: "They have fixed some areas. The midfield engine room is stronger with [Sandro] Tonali and [Mateus] Fernandes, [Rodrigo] Bentancur. That's a strong midfield. Conor Gallagher could have started. I don't think midfield is a big problem.

- Tottenham 2-3 Aston Villa: Sorry Spurs beaten despite finally scoring

- Tottenham vs Aston Villa: Spurs fall to another home defeat despite late consolations - as it happened

"They are weak and flaky at the back, and concede too many goals. A straight, long ball? If your two centre-backs can't deal with that, you are going to have problems. That needs to be fixed.

"They haven't got a poacher, they haven't got a goalscorer. I say that respectfully because they have good players, exciting players, in the frontline. But who's going to get 20 goals?

"If you haven't got that, and you concede goals at the back, it might be time to get concerned for Spurs fans."

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi refuses to speak to Tottenham players, calls on 'leaders' to 'lead'
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi called on the "leaders" in the Tottenham squad to "lead the team" as he criticised the manner in which they conceded the first two of Aston Villa's goals.
articles.headlineJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ、トッテナムの選手たちとの会話を拒否し、「リーダー」に「チームを引っ張ること」を求める
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ監督はアストン・ヴィラ戦での最初の2失点の仕方を批判し、トッテナムのスカッドの「リーダー」たちに「チームを牽引する」よう求めた。
articles.body:
LONDON -- Roberto De Zerbi called on the "leaders" in the Tottenham squad to "lead the team" as he criticised the manner in which they conceded the first two of Aston Villa's goals during the visitors' 3-2 win in north London on Saturday.

Goals from Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia proved too much for Spurs to overcome despite a late second-half fightback from Spurs which saw them score their first and second goals of the Premier League season.

This is Spurs' worst start to a Premier League season after five games, with two points and a goal difference of -6, eclipsing their poor start to the 2008-09 campaign (two points, -3 goal difference).

Spurs were on top in the opening exchanges but missed several presentable opportunities to open the scoring and were ultimately punished for their profligacy when Manzambi broke the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

His goal came seconds after play was restarted following Micky van de Ven's facial injury which saw him leave the pitch for further treatment. With their captain off the pitch, Spurs' 10-men duly conceded a sloppy goal.

Things got worse in the second half after Mohammed Kudus had an equaliser ruled out for offside in the build-up when Jackson doubled Villa's lead thanks to some poor Spurs defending.

"I don't want to speak about the first half," De Zerbi told a post-match news conference. "When we dominate the game, we create more chances to score. We play well. I want to speak why or better. I don't want to speak, but my focus is why we concede the first goal [when we have] 10 players just for one minute.

"In that situation we can stay stronger, we can communicate more and more and more. We can defend in a compact way. I put Bentancur as a centre-back in that minute and Mateus Fernandes as a midfielder. So if we bring a red card, we can play 40 minutes, 70 minutes, 60 minutes with 10 players and what is the problem?

"And then in the second half we scored the goal with Kudus offside. I don't know if some players lost energy, but we conceded one unacceptable goal from a goal kick."

De Zerbi cut a frustrated figure on the sideline for much of the contest, pulling his t-shirt over his face as his players failed to find the back of the net in the first half and sitting with his hands on his head in the dugout as Villa took control of the match in the second.

The Italian continued: "We knew before the game because this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season. And we spoke in many, many meetings yesterday and two days ago.

"To that we have to explain another game like Newcastle where we played the first half well, 60 minutes OK. And then we lose for sure... it is my responsibility... I take my responsibility. In the Premier League, Saturday's action began with Aston Villa beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-2 in London. Both teams were chasing their first league victory of the season and, while Spurs are still winless and in the bottom three, they did score their first goals on the campaign.

Next up, Brighton & Hove Albion host leaders and defending champions Arsenal in a clash between two teams near the top of the table. Finally, Nottingham Forest host a Coventry City side still searching for their first win and goal of the season.

Elsewhere, AS Roma host Inter Milan in a huge clash between Serie A's current top two. In the Bundesliga, Stuttgart take on Borussia Dortmund, while in LaLiga, Sevilla host league leaders Barcelona.

Sept. 19: Saturday morning's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's action starts a bit earlier than initially scheduled, with the Windy City doubling as Rainy City. To avoid heavy showers in the early evening, the Chicago White Sox hosting the Detroit Tigers has been moved up to 2:10 p.m. ET. Three more matinees follow in the 4:00 p.m. ET block, leaving 11 evening games.

The Boston Red Sox have not quite yet secured a playoff berth, but they're adjusting their rotation for the impending wild-card round by sending Brayan Bello to the hill today to face the Tampa Bay Rays in St. Petersburg. A Red Sox win alone doesn't clinch a postseason spot, but a win combined with a Texas Rangers loss, or if the Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays and the Atlanta Braves defeat the Houston Astros, the Red Sox will make the wild-card round for the second straight season.

The New York Yankees are set to place Aaron Judge on the 10-day IL due to a right calf strain. Backdating the visit to Wednesday will allow the slugger to return for the last day of the season, though it's unclear if he'll be ready. His playoff availability is also in jeopardy. Heliot Ramos will likely see more action in right field.

Hunter Goodman rejoined the Colorado Rockies lineup after missing four of the past five games. He's been nursing a sore thumb. Goodman enters the weekend leading all catchers in home runs with 38.

Dansby Swanson was reinstated from the injured list in advance of last night's game between the Chicago Cubs and Cincinnati Reds. The slick-fielding shortstop's return pushed Nico Hoerner back to second base. Swanson is two home runs and three steals away from a 20/20 season, but his .217 batting average is by far the lowest of his career.

The St. Louis Cardinals will have to play the rest of the season without Joshua Baez. He was placed on the 10-day IL with a strained left oblique. Technically, he can return for the final game of the season, but chances are he won't be ready.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Saturday.

articles.headline: José Mourinho rejects Real Madrid, Barcelona comparisons: LaLiga 'a marathon'
articles.description: José Mourinho has rejected comparisons between his Real Madrid team and high-scoring Barcelona, saying the LaLiga season is "a marathon" ahead of Sunday's Madrid Derby.
articles.headlineJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョ、レアル・マドリードとバルセロナの比較を否定：ラ・リーガは「マラソン」
articles.descriptionJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョ監督は日曜日のマドリード・ダービーを前に、ラ・リーガのシーズンは「マラソン」であると述べ、自身のレアル・マドリードと量産型のバルセロナとの比較を否定した。
articles.body:
José Mourinho has rejected comparisons between his Real Madrid team and high-scoring Barcelona, saying the LaLiga season is "a marathon" ahead of Sunday's Madrid Derby.

Title rivals Barcelona have scored 28 goals in six league games -- including Wednesday's 7-2 thrashing of Racing Santander -- and are three points clear of Real, as Mourinho's side prepare to visit Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano.

Madrid have lost just once, 1-0 at Real Betis, but have twice needed dramatic late goals to secure three points, most recently with Carlos Espí's 91st minute winner away at Elche this week.

"Historically, culturally, Real Madrid can't be compared to anyone," Mourinho said, when asked if he was worried by Barça's displays so far.

"So I won't compare us to any team. I'll speak about us, our problems, and the things we have to improve. In the few months I've been here, I understand that it's more difficult all the time to hear something positive about Real Madrid.

"We're aware of the problems we have, but we're also very aware of the power we have, individually and collectively, of the very good things we have in our team. In the three games where we've got to the final minutes needing to score, we finished with an effort -- physical and psychological -- and determination.

"Apart from quality, this team has strength as a group. It's a marathon. The league isn't always a straight motorway, without obstacles. But we'll be there."

- Real Madrid win U20 cup, three red cards for Santiago Wanderers

- Mbappé: I want to bring Ballon d'Or to Bernabéu despite boos

- Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike and signs with sponsor On

Mourinho acknowledged that his team have struggled to perform over 90 minutes so far this season, such as in the Elche game, where they led 2-0 only to concede twice late on, forcing a frantic push for a winner.

"This is a process," Mourinho said. "If coaches train for two, three, four, five, or ten years, and they talk about a process and evolution, imagine when we've been together for just a few months."

Mourinho praised his opposite number Simeone, who has been in charge at Atletico ever since Mourinho's first spell at the Bernabéu.

"You say so many silly things in your career," Mourinho said, when asked about past comments on Simeone. "Sometimes you're affected by the moment and sometimes it's strategic. But in the end, you respect, or you don't ... We're rivals again, but we're war comrades."

articles.headline: Drab Tottenham fall to Aston Villa loss despite ending goalless run
articles.description: Aston Villa piled the pressure on big-spending Tottenham and Roberto De Zerbi with a 3-2 away victory to claim a first win in the Premier League this season.
articles.headlineJa: 低調なトッテナム、無得点に終止符を打つもアストン・ヴィラに敗北
articles.descriptionJa: アストン・ヴィラは敵地で3-2の勝利を収めて今季プレミアリーグ初勝利を挙げ、大型補強を行ったトッテナムとロベルト・デ・ツェルビ監督への圧力を強めた。
articles.body:
Aston Villa piled the pressure on big-spending Tottenham and Roberto De Zerbi with a 3-2 away victory to claim a first win in the Premier League this season.

Both clubs had made slow starts to the new campaign after summer rebuilds and while Spurs had failed to score in four league fixtures, there had been green shoots in 0-0 draws with Nottingham Forest and Everton.

However, Tottenham's latest strong opening was again followed by a meek collapse after Johan Manzambi broke the deadlock in first-half added-time when he tapped in Boubacar Kamara's cross.

It occurred with Spurs captain Micky van de Ven off the pitch receiving treatment, but boss De Zerbi watched the hosts produce a disjoined second-half performance and conceded again in the 67th minute through Nicolas Jackson.

A superb long-range strike by Emi Buendia with 11 minutes left made the points safe for Unai Emery's Villa before Conor Gallagher ended Tottenham's league goal drought with a close-range finish after 87 minutes.

Jan Paul van Hecke headed a second late on but this latest defeat was greeted with boos, with patience starting to wear thin after a summer of lavish spending.

articles.headline: Chelsea 'hurt' by Brentford thumping - Levi Colwill
articles.description: Levi Colwill said Chelsea were left "hurt" by the margin of defeat as they were thumped 3-0 by Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.
articles.headlineJa: ブレントフォード戦の大敗にチェルシーは「傷ついている」 — レヴィ・コルウィル
articles.descriptionJa: Gtechコミュニティ・スタジアムでブレントフォードに0-3で完敗を喫し、レヴィ・コルウィルはチェルシーがその点差での敗戦に「傷ついた」と語った。
articles.body:
Levi Colwill said Chelsea were left "hurt" by the margin of defeat as they were thumped 3-0 by Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The visitors were much improved defensively in the first half following some shaky displays, looking not half as chaotic at the back and in midfield as they have done at times this season.

Everything then changed when poor making at a corner in the 61st minute allowed Jaidon Anthony to head in unmarked from virtually on the goal-line before further goals from Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho condemned the Blues to a hiding.

"It was tough," Colwill said. "Conceding from a set-piece isn't the best and then we tried to push and maybe over-exposed ourselves and played some passes we shouldn't and forced it.

"I feel we needed to relax and not push too hard for the equaliser. We needed to believe it would come if we continued playing our football. But I think we pushed too hard to get it and they hurt us on the counter.

"They get the second goal and then the third goal really hit home and hurt. The second half we weren't good enough, obviously and we've got a lot to work on during the international break."

Chelsea's excellent goal-scoring form was brought to an abrupt end as Brentford marshalled their injury-hit forward line superbly.

The absence up front of João Pedro was hard to ignore, his replacement Danny Welbeck not quite so able to act as the middle link in a fluid trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

Both forwards were involved and looked dangerous, but they operated far less in combination than when Pedro is present.

It left Xabi Alonso's side, who had scored 18 times in six matches in all competitions ahead of Friday's west London derby, looking strangely out of sorts, with little apparent attacking threat.

"We can't rely on the front three to pull us out of danger," Colwill said. "The rest of us have to try to help as much as possible. The defence, the midfield and the attackers, we all need to help each other much more.

"We've definitely got a lot of room to improve."

 - Xabi Alonso joins unwanted managerial group after heavy Brentford defeat

- Xabi Alonso says Chelsea were 'out of control' in Brentford loss

- How can erratic Chelsea find stability? For starters: Look to Brentford

The result left Alonso as only the sixth manager in Premier League history have two or more goals scored against his side in each of his first five matches.

Previously only Mick McCarthy, Sammy Lee, Terry Connor, Slavisa Jokanovic and Scott Parker had begun life in the division with such frailty at the back.

Brentford were rampant after going in front. In the 83rd minute, Kevin Schade ran clear and was denied by Emiliano Martínez, but there to knock in his first league goal of the season on the rebound was Thiago.

Substitute Carvalho made it three in stoppage time from Schade's cross.
